Package sc.fiji.snt.gui

Class FileDrop

java.lang.Object
sc.fiji.snt.gui.FileDrop
public class FileDrop extends Object
Makes it easy to drag and drop files from the operating system to a Java program. Any Component displayed in a Swing window can be dropped onto. While dragging, a frame is painted over the target without affecting its border or layout.

To use this class, construct a new FileDrop by passing it the target component and a FileDrop.Listener to receive notification when file(s) have been dropped. Dropped files are delivered on the Event Dispatch Thread, after the drop operation has been completed, so listeners are free to display dialogs or start long running tasks. Example: 

 new FileDrop(myPanel, files -> {
     // handle file drop
 });

Released into the Public Domain by the original author, Robert Harder (rob@iharder.net).

Additional support:

  • September 2007, Nathan Blomquist: Linux (KDE/Gnome) support
  • December 2010, Joshua Gerth
  • June 2019, TF: Adjusted default border color, code cleanup
  • 2026, TF: Modernization (single drop handler, headless awareness, uri-list parsing, asynchronous listener dispatch, uninstall support, layout neutral drag highlight)

      public FileDrop(Component c, FileDrop.Listener listener)

    • FileDrop

      public FileDrop(Component c, boolean recursive, FileDrop.Listener listener)
      Constructs a FileDrop. In headless mode this constructor is a no-op.
      Parameters:
      c - the component on which files will be dropped
      recursive - if true, and c is a Container, its children will also be set as drop targets, though only c is highlighted while dragging
      listener - notified when files are dropped

  • Method Details

    • uninstall

      public void uninstall()
      Removes the drag-and-drop hooks installed by this instance, restoring any drop target the components had before. Call this if you add and remove components after you've set up the drag-and-drop.
